newsitem.title: SPAIN: Thousands protest throughout Spain against rebels.
newsitem.headline: Thousands protest throughout Spain against rebels.

text.p: Thousands of people took to the streets throughout Spain on Sunday in a protest against the separatist group ETA and calling for the release of two men believed to be held by the group, Spanish media reported.

In the Basque country more than 20,000 people marched through Vizcaya demanding an end to the Basque separatists' campaign of violence which took a new turn earlier this week with the alleged kidnap of a businessman.

Protestors demanded the release of prison officer Jose Antonio Ortega Lara who was kidnapped by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) in January and Basque businessman Cosme Delclaux who went missing on Monday.
Although ETA have not confirmed they abducted Delclaux, Spain's government said earlier in the week it appeared that he had been kidnapped by the Basque rebels.
Basque regional government interior minister Juan Maria Atutxa also accused the rebel group of kidnapping Delclaux during demonstrations on Sunday.
Local media said Delclaux's disappearance had coincided with a new campaign of extortion by ETA which in the past few weeks, had sent letters to about 50 businessmen demanding money.
The Basque separatists have killed nearly 800 people in a drive for full independence since 1968.
